$comment: Maps every implemented feature to the specification clause that defines it, and records the test that proves the implementation matches. 'implemented: false' entries are the explicit non-claims — constructs the specs define that this package deliberately does not emit.

requirements.requirement: A bare identifier declares a node with no text.
Bracket forms select node shape: [] () ([]) {} {{}} [[]] (()).
Characters that break syntax are escaped as #NNN; or by HTML character name; # itself is #35;.
Normal, dotted and thick links with arrow heads.
A link may be drawn without an arrow head: A --- B, A -.- B, A === B.
requirements.reason: Every edge this package emits is directed, so an undirected link would misrepresent the data. FlowchartEdge has no arrow parameter.

requirements.clause: A link with arrow head and text
requirements.requirement: Edge labels use the pipe form: A -->|text| B.
TB, TD, BT, RL, LR declared on the flowchart statement.
subgraph id["title"] ... end, grouping member nodes.
requirements.note: The flowchart lexer matches the 'direction' keyword inside a quoted subgraph title, so the word is escaped there; the same text in a node or edge label needs no such treatment.

requirements.requirement: A node is named by an identifier, which the renderer emits unquoted.
requirements.note: Identifiers cannot be escaped, so they are validated instead. The accepted character set and the list of reserved words were both established by testing candidate identifiers against the Mermaid parser.

requirements.requirement: A state is declared bare or with a description after a colon.
A state whose description contains spaces is defined with an id first: state "description" as id.
From --> To, optionally with : text.
[*] denotes the start and end pseudo-states.
A state may be declared as a bare id, as 'id : description', or as 'state "description" as id'. The renderer emits exactly one declaration per state, choosing the form the label requires.
requirements.note: Every state is declared, including one whose label equals its id. Such a state is mentioned nowhere else in the output, so omitting the bare-id line dropped it from the diagram silently; with a note attached the result parsed but failed to render.

requirements.clause: Setting the direction of the diagram
requirements.requirement: direction TB | BT | RL | LR. TD is not documented for state diagrams.
note left of | right of {id} : text.
requirements.note: Only the single-line form. The multi-line 'note right of X\n ... \nend note' block form is not emitted. The position is restricted to the two words the clause defines; any other value is a Mermaid lexical error.

requirements.requirement: A transition label and a note body are introduced by ':' and have no quoted form, so a colon in the text is read as grammar.
requirements.note: Verified against the Mermaid parser: '::' in a transition label is read as the class-application operator, and any colon in a note body is a parse error.

requirements.requirement: ';' separates statements, so text containing one is read as further diagram source rather than as part of the label.
requirements.note: The prose does not state this; it was derived from the parser, which accepted a label of 'do x; then A --> B' by silently adding two states and a transition the caller never asked for. Unlike the colon it also applies to the quoted 'state "..." as id' form, so it is escaped in every state text position; '#59;' was confirmed by render to draw as ';'. The flowchart grammar quotes its label positions and needs no equivalent escape - also proven by render.

requirements.requirement: A state is named by an identifier, which the renderer emits unquoted.
requirements.note: Identifiers cannot be escaped, so they are validated instead: an id containing an arrow or a newline would otherwise inject extra states and transitions into an output that still parses.

requirements.requirement: state X { ... } nests a state machine inside a state.
requirements.reason: MermaidState has no child-state slot, so there is nothing in the data model to nest. Adding it would change the public type.

requirements.requirement: state X <<choice>> models a branch point.
requirements.reason: Not represented in the data model; a LinkML schema expresses the same thing as guarded transitions, which are supported.

requirements.requirement: state X <<fork>> / <<join>> model concurrent splits.
requirements.reason: Not represented in the data model.

requirements.requirement: -- separates concurrent regions inside a composite state.
requirements.reason: Depends on composite states, which are not implemented.

requirements.requirement: classDef and class statements style states.
requirements.reason: Styling is a presentation concern the caller can append to the rendered output.

requirements.requirement: Header row, delimiter row, data rows; cells delimited by pipes.
A leading or trailing colon in the delimiter row sets left, right or centre alignment.
A pipe in cell content must be escaped, including inside other inline spans.
A bare 'www.' token, a 'scheme://' URL and a bare email address are linkified without any active character being present.
requirements.note: 'scheme://' is defeated by the ':' escape. The 'www.' form contains no active character, so the dot after 'www' is escaped instead. The bare email form is a documented limit: in cmark-gfm neither backslash escaping nor a character reference suppresses it.

requirements.requirement: A cell holds inline content only; the table ends at the first blank line or block structure.
Backtick-delimited inline code; the delimiter run must be longer than any backtick run in the content.
One space is stripped from each end of a span that both begins and ends with a space, unless the content consists entirely of spaces.
requirements.note: The renderer adds compensating padding so a value keeps its leading and trailing spaces, which matters for indented lines of multi-line code. The all-spaces carve-out is the one case the rule declines to undo, so such a value would come back wider than it went in; it emits no span at all instead.

requirements.requirement: *text* is emphasis, **text** is strong emphasis; a delimiter run adjacent to whitespace cannot open or close one.
Any ASCII punctuation may be backslash-escaped, but backslash escapes do not work inside code spans.
Annotations are arbitrary key-value pairs attached to schema elements.
A class acquires slots from inline attributes, from named top-level slots, and by inheritance; annotations must be read from all three.
requirements.note: Reading ClassDefinition.attributes alone sees only inline attributes, so a schema written in LinkML's top-level 'slots:' style, or one using 'is_a' inheritance, would silently expose no annotated slots at all.
